d65911d574.q: What was Ron Johnson's strategy to differentiate Target from Walmart in the 1990s?
d65911d574.a: Johnson launched the first ever designer partnership with architect Michael Graves, creating 140 high-quality home products for Target at $25-30 price points, positioning Target as offering better design than Walmart while maintaining competitive pricing. He believed the opportunity was not just to be different than Walmart, but to deliver merchandise quality found in specialty stores like Crate and Barrel at substantially better prices, capturing higher wallet share from customers.

ccdf785848.q: Why did Steve Jobs decide Apple needed its own retail stores instead of selling through Best Buy or CompUSA?
ccdf785848.a: Steve Jobs concluded his number one weakness was go-to-market strategy and lacked advocacy for Apple products at point of sale. Traditional channels like Best Buy and CompUSA employed staff who loved PCs and would discourage customers from buying Macs, saying they were twice as expensive, lacked software, and had slower processors. Jobs realized he needed his own stores to have a chance to win and reach customers hand-to-hand.

e9e782a494.q: What was the core problem the Apple Store design aimed to solve when it opened?
e9e782a494.a: The core problem was overcoming people's fear of technology, not just getting their hands on a Mac. Johnson and Jobs recognized they needed to reach non-computer buyers by locating stores in malls where people already shopped, then hiring commission-free staff who could interact with tech novices, provide hands-on experience with products, and offer services like theaters, one-to-one training tables, and the Genius Bar to build confidence.

266e183510.q: How did Ron Johnson convince Target leadership to invest in higher-priced designer merchandise while competing against Walmart?
266e183510.a: Johnson did detailed merchandising homework showing that Target carried 30 toasters priced between $9.99 and $15, creating confusion, while Walmart only carried 25 in similar price points. By reallocating just 10% of merchandise to higher-priced beautiful items through one major designer partnership, Target could differentiate without losing competitive positioning. Johnson emphasized that differentiation strategy must make something both different and better to create preference, not just different.

d532fa6e19.q: What was Ron Johnson's key insight about Apple's market opportunity when Steve Jobs asked him to double market share?
d532fa6e19.a: Johnson told Jobs that thinking only about competing with Microsoft's entrenched position was wrong. Instead, he argued that half the people in the country had never owned a computer—they were at halftime. Eventually everyone would have computers, so Apple should go after everybody and win the second half, rather than just trying to convert existing computer buyers who preferred PCs.
